_comment: Billing multipliers used to collapse the input token classes into one
comparable number, `weighted tokens`. Relative to uncached input at 1.0.
These live in data rather than in code so a pricing change is an edit
here, not a release. `flow cost trend` reads them at run time.
They are Anthropic's cache multipliers and are applied to Claude rows
only. Codex reports no cache-write tokens at all (zero across 16,260 rows
on the corpus this was built against) and its `cached_input_tokens` is a
SUBSET of `input_tokens` where Claude's cache buckets are disjoint and
additive — the same arithmetic would mean something different per
harness, so the weighted columns are blank for Codex rather than wrong.
cache_write_unsplit is the fallback for a row harvested before Claude's
`usage.cache_creation` TTL breakdown existed, where only the write total
is known. It is deliberately the 5m rate — the cheaper of the two — so an
unknown split under-weights rather than over-weights. Zero such rows exist
on this corpus after the schema v5 backfill; it is here so a restored old
store degrades honestly instead of silently counting every legacy write at
Verified against Anthropic's published cache pricing 2026-08-15.
